questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: ______ the source of a malfunction in a complex electrical system can be a painstaking, time-consuming process: a repair technician may need to test each individual component one by one until the specific part causing the problematic behavior is identified.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Testing components one by one until the faulty part is found describes isolating (singling out) the source of the problem. Adapting, incorporating and fabricating don't describe finding a cause.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Single-celled foraminifera inhabiting coastal waters experience significant environmental salinity changes during tidal cycles. How, then, do they ______ internal salt levels? Some organisms maintain high concentrations of phosphates that allow them to affect the concentration of internal electrolytes—including salt—in response to external changes. It may be that coastal foraminifera do the same.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: The text describes organisms adjusting their internal salt concentration in response to outside changes, which is regulating it. They don't counteract or elude their own salt levels, and "tolerate" misses the idea of active control.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Though most studies of the effect of altitude on blood chemistry usually concentrate on people who live above sea level, researchers Suleiman A. Al-Sweedan and Moath Alhaj have instead chosen the ______ path in their recent work of studying the blood of people who live below sea level, in locations such as the California towns of Westmorland and Thermal.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: "Instead" contrasts the researchers with most studies: studying people below sea level is a new, innovative approach. Predictable and timeworn say the opposite, and nothing suggests the path is idealistic.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: While once ______, basic computer security training that only teaches recognition of obvious scams cannot provide enough protection against today’s sophisticated fake emails, which employ such subtle deception techniques that many organizations now require their staff to complete comprehensive cybersecurity education programs.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: "While once" sets up a contrast with "cannot provide enough protection" now, so the training was once sufficient. The contrast is about whether it's enough, not how common, deep or cheap it was.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: The architectural firm’s design for the new municipal library was deliberately ______; by rejecting ornate embellishments in favor of clean lines and unadorned surfaces, the architects prioritized utility and simplicity over grandeur.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Rejecting ornament for clean, unadorned surfaces and simplicity is an austere (plain, severe) design. Ostentatious and convoluted are the opposite, and capricious means unpredictable.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: What is a city? The answer depends on where you live! Many countries define an area as a city based on how many people live there. However, not every country uses the same numbers. Iceland defines a city as an area with a population of at least 200, while the Netherlands defines a city as having a minimum population of 20,000. Some countries even define cities using other factors, like if there is a local government.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It lists the number of cities in one country, then compares that number to the number of cities in another country.
It poses a question, then explains why the question has many answers.
It offers a recommendation, then provides reasons for that recommendation.
It describes two locations, then explains why only one of the locations is considered a city.

questions.explanation: The text opens with "What is a city?" and then shows that the answer varies: different population cut-offs and other factors in different countries. It never counts cities, recommends anything or compares two specific places.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from the 1940 novel The Hamlet by William Faulkner. In rural Mississippi, a man is riding a horse toward the residence of a man he intends to meet about a business matter.

He was breathing hard but not because he had been galloping. On the contrary, since he had approached near enough to his destination to believe he could have seen smoke if there had been smoke, he had ridden slower and slower. Nevertheless he now sat the horse before the gap in the fence, breathing hard enough through his nose and even sweating a little, looking at the sagging broken-backed cabin set in its inevitable treeless and grassless plot and weathered to the color of an old bee-hive, with that expression of tense and rapid speculation of a man approaching a dud howitzer [artillery] shell.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.text: To contrast the man’s desire to attend the meeting with his awareness of the risk involved in attending it
To compare the upcoming meeting to a far more serious experience from earlier in the man’s life
To depict the man’s insistence on meeting despite the inconvenience of traveling on horseback
To portray the man’s anxiety about the meeting as reflected by his physical state and demeanor

questions.explanation: The man breathes hard though he hasn't galloped, sweats, slows down as he nears, and looks like someone approaching an unexploded shell: his body and expression show his anxiety. The shell is a comparison, not an earlier experience, and the text doesn't stress his desire to go or the ride's inconvenience.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: James Fong and his team claim to have discovered a new color, which they named olo. Olo is a very saturated blue-green color that can’t be seen with the human eye under natural conditions. In the human eye, long, medium, and short cones in the retina help sense bright light and color. Olo can only be seen by activating the medium cones alone. Fong and team activated these cones by using a targeted laser technology to stimulate just the medium cone cells.
questions.prompt: According to the text, how can the color olo be seen?

choices.text: By activating only the medium cones in the retina
By activating the long, medium, and short cones in the retina
By activating both the long and short cones in the retina
By activating only the long cones in the retina

questions.explanation: The text says directly that olo "can only be seen by activating the medium cones alone."

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: A student is collecting data about countries with volcanoes that have been active in the time since 1800 and in the time since 1960. The student records that Ethiopia has ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?

choices.text: the same number of volcanoes that have been active since 1800 as Tanzania has.
no volcanoes that have been active since 1800.
more volcanoes that have been active since 1960 than Tanzania has.
fewer volcanoes that have been active since 1960 than Tanzania has.

questions.explanation: Since 1960, Ethiopia has 5 active volcanoes and Tanzania has 1, so Ethiopia has more. Since 1800 the counts are 10 and 3, which rules out A and B, and D reverses the comparison.

images.alt: Bar graph, Volcanoes Active since 1800 and since 1960 in Two Countries. Active since 1800: Tanzania 3, Ethiopia 10. Active since 1960: Tanzania 1, Ethiopia 5.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Editor Jared Shurin’s enormous 2023 anthology The Big Book of Cyberpunk comprises 108 stories. Shurin’s volume is chronologically expansive, featuring such stories as James Tiptree Jr.’s “The Girl Who Was Plugged In” (1973) and Erica Satifka’s “Act of Providence” (2021). In his introduction, Shurin defines cyberpunk as a subgenre of speculative fiction concerning “the influence of technology on the scale, the pace, or the pattern of human affairs”; however, some critics assert that cyberpunk is a literary movement that is in large part aesthetic rather than idea driven.
questions.prompt: Which quotation from a literary critic would be the most effective evidence in support of the underlined claim?

choices.text: “Not all the stories anthologized in The Big Book of Cyberpunk were first published as stand-alone short stories in magazines or journals: for example, qntm’s 2021 story ‘Lena’ was originally self-published on the author’s site qntm.org.”

“The stories in The Big Book of Cyberpunk share a number of common themes indicative of cyberpunk as a whole: body modification; resistance to authority; the ways in which technological advancements alter human behavior.”
“Shurin’s characterization of cyberpunk is remarkably generous: it is a categorization that might well serve for the entire field of science fiction in general, rather than cyberpunk in particular.”

“A key component of cyberpunk that differentiates it from other subgenres of science fiction is an affection for the totems of 1980s pop culture, such as the mirrored sunglasses that were then popular.”

questions.explanation: The claim is that cyberpunk is defined mostly by its look and style rather than its ideas. D says what sets it apart is an affection for 1980s pop-culture items like mirrored sunglasses, which is an aesthetic trait. B stresses shared themes (ideas), C only criticizes Shurin's definition, and A is about publication history.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage:
Tribal nations employ a large percentage of their populations in tribally owned businesses as well as in government and public administration. This is especially true in Oklahoma and other states with robust tribal economies and large Native populations. Between end-of-year 2017 and end-of-year 2023, the percentage of tribal employees working in the public sector increased, from 34.0% to 34.6%, while the percentage working in the business sector declined from 66.0% to 65.4%.

Employment in Tribal Economies in December 2017 and December 2023 by Sector
