questions.prompt: Which statement about the decline in the percentage of tribal employees working in the business sector is best supported by information in the table?

choices.text: It didn’t result from an overall contraction of that sector, since the total number of employees in that sector increased by several thousand during this period.
It was offset by changes in leisure and hospitality businesses, since the percentage of employees working in those businesses increased during this period.
It was driven primarily by changes in businesses classified as “other,” since those businesses had the lowest number of employees by the end of 2023.
It resulted from widespread workforce redistributions, since several thousand employees left that sector to take new jobs in the public sector during this period.

questions.explanation: Business-sector employees rose from 220,700 to 232,300, an increase of about 11,600, so the share fell only because the public sector grew faster. B is wrong because leisure and hospitality's share fell (55.3% to 54.2%), C because "other" grew, and D because the table shows no one leaving the business sector.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: While US public charities, like Commonfund, must file Form 990 yearly with the IRS, private foundations, such as Lilly Endowment Inc., must file a different form, 990-PF. In addition, foundations that engage in certain prohibited activities must also file Form 4720 and pay an excise tax on the money involved. Private foundations are prohibited from holding excess interests in a business enterprise, “self-dealing” (conducting activities that benefit foundation insiders), making taxable expenditures such as grants to noncharitable entities, and failing to cross a required threshold in making charitable distributions from income. Out of the organizations that filed Form 990-PF in the years 2003–2005, ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the assertion?

choices.text: those that filed Form 4720 because they had excess holdings in a business enterprise paid, on average, a larger penalty than those that filed Form 4720 because they made taxable expenditures.
those that filed Form 4720 because they engaged in self-dealing paid an increasing percentage of the total penalty each year from 2003 to 2005.

those that filed Form 4720 in 2003 because they failed to meet the minimum charitable distribution requirement collectively paid a larger percentage of the total penalty assessed that year than those that filed Form 4720 in 2005 for the same reason.

those that filed Form 4720 in 2005 because they engaged in self-dealing collectively paid a larger percentage of the total penalty assessed that year than those that filed Form 990 but also filed Form 4720 for the same reason.

questions.explanation: Failing to meet the distribution requirement is the "undistributed income" category: about 79% of the total penalty in 2003 versus about 55% in 2005, so C is right. A asks about averages the graph doesn't show, B fails because self-dealing dropped from 2003 to 2004, and D is about Form 990 filers, who aren't in the graph.

images.alt: Bar graph, Tax Penalties Assessed on Private Foundations That Filed Form 4720, by Reason, 2003–2005, as a percentage of the total penalty. Self-dealing: about 10% (2003), 6% (2004), 40% (2005). Undistributed income: about 79%, 77%, 55%. Taxable expenditures: about 7%, 14%, 4%. Excess business holdings: about 3%, 4%, 1%.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Philoctetes is a play by Sophocles that was first performed in 409 BCE. In the play, Odysseus and Neoptolemus must retrieve Philoctetes—a master archer who is believed necessary for the Greeks to win the Trojan War—from a cave on a deserted island where Odysseus and others had abandoned him with a debilitating injury earlier in the war. Odysseus suggests that the plan for returning with Philoctetes rests on Neoptolemus not having been part of the group that abandoned him: ______
questions.prompt: Which quotation from Philoctetes most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.text: “Since the prize of victory is so dear, / Endure it [acting deceitfully]—We’ll be just another day / But now, for one brief hour, devote thyself / To serve me without shame.”

“Go near now silently, and make me know / If still he persevere, and hold this spot, / Or have roamed elsewhere, that informed of this / I may proceed with what remains to say, / And we may act in concert.”

“Now let me show, why thine approach to him / Is safe and trustful as mine cannot be / Thou didst sail forth, not to redeem thine oath, / Nor by constraint, nor with the foremost band. / All which reproaches I must bear.”
“No moment for this talk, / Lest he discern my coming, and I lose / The scheme, wherewith I think to catch him soon.”

questions.explanation: In C, Odysseus explains that Neoptolemus can approach Philoctetes safely because he didn't sail "with the foremost band" (the group that abandoned him), while Odysseus must bear the blame. The other quotations are about deceit, scouting or secrecy, not Neoptolemus's absence from that group.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Louis-Ferdinand Céline’s 1932 novel Journey to the End of the Night is regularly described as autobiographical. That characterization is apt—there are many parallels between the experiences of the novel’s protagonist, Ferdinand Bardamu, and those of Céline—but it should not be taken to mean that every person or event depicted in Journey to the End of the Night has a real-life analogue. Much of the novel is pure invention, and readers who ignore this fact and instead focus excessively on correspondences between the novel and Céline’s life can thus ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: fail to appreciate how much creativity Céline shows in the book.
overemphasize the extent to which Céline took inspiration from earlier writers.
refuse to acknowledge that Céline drew on real-world material when writing Journey to the End of the Night.
misrepresent Journey to the End of the Night as being more widely read than it actually is.

questions.explanation: Since much of the novel is pure invention, readers who treat it all as autobiography miss what Céline invented, his creativity. The text doesn't discuss earlier writers or readership, and such readers over-acknowledge, not deny, the real-world material.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Ecologist Dr. Elena Vance observed that urban wetlands filter pollutants at rates comparable to modern treatment facilities. However, Vance cautions that overloading these fragile ecosystems with industrial runoff can degrade their microbial communities, ultimately compromising their filtration efficiency. Without strict municipal regulations on chemical discharge, the natural buffering capacity of such wetlands could permanently diminish.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the primary function of the underlined sentence in the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It introduces a technical method for measuring chemical pollutants in urban watersheds.
It qualifies the earlier praise of wetlands by noting a condition under which their benefits are compromised.
It dismisses artificial wastewater treatment facilities as ineffective alternatives.
It refutes a prevailing hypothesis regarding microbial diversity in aquatic environments.

questions.explanation: The first sentence praises wetlands' filtering; the underlined sentence, opening with "However," limits that praise by saying overloading them with runoff harms their filtering. It doesn't describe a method, criticize treatment plants or refute a hypothesis.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: With an average summer temperature of 82.5 degrees Fahrenheit, Nicosia is one European ______ many travelers recommend, especially from June to September.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "That many travelers recommend" is a restrictive clause identifying which city, so it takes "that" with no comma. "That" is never preceded by a comma in this use, "which" with a comma makes the clause nonessential, and "in which" doesn't fit "recommend."

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Nanoengineers have developed synthesized mesoporous silica nanoparticles that are used to transport genes and medicines to specific cells in the body. As nanotechnology evolves, medical technology ______ to evolve as well.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "As nanotechnology evolves" is in the present, describing an ongoing process, so the result is in the future: "will likely continue." The past perfect and conditional forms don't match the present-tense clause.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: To more easily balance the weight of her body on her toes while performing the demanding pointe work that became increasingly common in early 20th-century ballet, internationally known ballerina Anna Pavlova redesigned her pointe shoes. The modifications she made—adding a stiffened leather sole and hardened toe ______ began the modernization of ballet’s iconic footwear.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The interruption opened with a dash after "made," so it must close with a matching dash before the verb "began."

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Archaeological evidence indicates that board games have existed in human societies for at least five millennia, with examples discovered in the tombs of ancient Egypt and the ruins of Mesopotamia. The purpose of these ancient games was ______ provide entertainment during leisure time, to reflect cultural beliefs, and to develop strategic thinking skills among players.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "The purpose of these ancient games was threefold" is a complete clause, and a colon properly introduces the list that explains it. A period or semicolon would leave a fragment, and no punctuation runs the list into "threefold."

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Extensive radiocarbon dating of reed samples from Caral confirmed Ruth Shady Solís’s hypothesis about the Peruvian site’s ______ nearly 5,000 years ago, the ancient city preceded the Olmec civilization to the north by a full millennium, a revelation that fundamentally altered our understanding of urban development in the Western Hemisphere.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Both sides are complete: what was confirmed, then an explanation of it (the city, built nearly 5,000 years ago, preceded the Olmec). A colon joins a clause to the explanation that follows. A comma alone would be a comma splice, and no punctuation runs them together.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Chemists investigating the properties of coal tar in the mid-nineteenth century discovered compounds that led to the creation of vibrant artificial colorants. Commercial applications of this new synthetic dye technology—beginning with the purple dye called mauve, discovered by William Perkin in 1856—______ responsible for launching what one science historian calls a “manufacturing revolution based on chemistry.”
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject is the plural "applications" (the words between the dashes don't change it), and the events are in the past, so the verb is "were."

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: How does a clear evening become foggy? First, the ground releases heat, which radiates upward. This causes the air near the ground to cool. ______ tiny water droplets begin to form as the cooling air reaches its dew point and can no longer hold its moisture as invisible vapor. Finally, as more droplets accumulate, a visible layer of fog develops close to the ground.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The text lists steps in order, "First … Finally," and the droplets forming is the middle step, so "Next" fits. "Lastly" can't come before "Finally."

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Scientists studying forest restoration have discovered that trees depend on complex partnerships with microscopic organisms for survival. The researchers found that special fungi called endophytes live inside tree leaves and serve as a defense mechanism. ______ these endophytes help by fighting off diseases and boosting the tree’s immune system.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The last sentence gives the details of how the endophytes act as a defense mechanism, so "Specifically" fits. There's no contrast or alternative, and it isn't a conclusion.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Pistol shrimp are small marine crustaceans that hunt using a specialized oversized claw.
• When the claw snaps shut rapidly, it pushes water through a narrow groove at extreme speed.
• This high-speed water jet creates a bubble that pops forcefully near the shrimp’s prey.
• The popping bubble generates shock waves powerful enough to stun small fish.
questions.prompt: The student wants to introduce pistol shrimp to an audience unfamiliar with these crustaceans. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: Some crustaceans use a specialized claw to create high-speed water jets and a bubble that stuns the small fish they prey on.
Pistol shrimp are small marine creatures that use a specialized oversized claw to generate shock waves powerful enough to stun small fish.
Pushing water through a narrow groove at extreme speeds, the snapping shut of the shrimp’s claw sets the shock-wave hunting process in motion.
Pistol shrimp are preyed on by small marine crustaceans that create high-speed water jets to stun their prey.

questions.explanation: B names pistol shrimp, says what they are and gives their most striking trait, which suits readers who don't know them. A never names them, C assumes the reader already knows "the shrimp," and D gets the facts wrong.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Chapantongo is a municipality in the state of Hidalgo, Mexico.
• Municipalities are governmental regions responsible for providing many public services to their residents.
• One service they provide is traffic control.
• Chapantongo’s population was 12,967 in 2020.
• Its population was 12,271 in 2010.
• Hidalgo is divided into 84 municipalities.
questions.prompt: The student wants to emphasize the 2020 population of Chapantongo. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: As of 2020, Chapantongo was one of 84 municipalities in Hidalgo, Mexico.
In 2020, the municipality of Chapantongo had a population of 12,967.
As a municipality in Hidalgo, Chapantongo is responsible for providing public services to its population.
Home to 12,271 people, the governmental region was responsible for providing traffic control to its population in 2010.

questions.explanation: Only B gives the 2020 population, 12,967. D gives the 2010 figure, and A and C give no population.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Future of Nostalgia is a scholarly book by literary theorist Svetlana Boym.
• The book explores the concept of nostalgia from various angles.
• Chapter 8 explores nostalgia and Europe’s largest shopping mall.
• Chapter 17 discusses various skeptics’ takes on the concept of nostalgia.
• In chapter 17, Boym writes, “The poethics of nostalgia combines estrangement and human solidarity, affect and reflection.”
questions.prompt: The student wants to explain what Svetlana Boym writes about in chapter 8. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: Svetlana Boym’s The Future of Nostalgia explores the concept of nostalgia from various angles.
As Svetlana Boym writes in the seventeenth chapter of her book, “The poethics of nostalgia combines estrangement and human solidarity, affect and reflection.”
Literary theorist Svetlana Boym explores nostalgia and Europe’s largest shopping mall in chapter 8 of her book.
After exploring nostalgia and Europe’s largest shopping mall, Svetlana Boym goes on to discuss various skeptics’ takes on the concept of nostalgia.

questions.explanation: C names chapter 8 and says what it covers. A is about the whole book, B is about chapter 17, and D focuses on what comes after chapter 8 without naming it.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: For decades, historical linguists hypothesized that Proto-Indo-European originated in the Pontic-Caspian steppe roughly 6,000 years ago. ______, recent ancient genomic analyses combined with phylogenetic linguistic modeling have provided compelling evidence supporting an earlier agricultural origin south of the Caucasus.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The new evidence points to a different origin from the long-held hypothesis, a contrast, so "However" fits.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage:
The following text is from Jacqueline Woodson’s 2018 novel Harbor Me.

I’ve pulled the voice recorder from my closet and have it sitting on the middle of my bed now. When I press play, Esteban’s voice fills my room.
questions.prompt: As used in the text, what does the word “pulled” most nearly mean?
questions.explanation: The narrator took the recorder out of the closet and put it on the bed, so "pulled" means taken.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: The National Heritage Fellowship was created to honor exceptional folk and traditional artists in the United States. One artist who received the fellowship is Mexican American rodeo tailor Manuel Cuevas. Cuevas was chosen for his lifetime ______ the arts.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: An honor for exceptional artists is given for a lifetime of contributions to the arts. The other choices are negative and wouldn't earn an honor.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Car manufacturers increasingly label certain vehicle components as “lifetime” parts that supposedly never need replacement. Mechanics tend to greet such assertions ______, as ample experience has shown them that environmental factors, varied driving conditions, and intensive use will likely lead to the eventual failure of these components.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Experience tells mechanics these parts will eventually fail, so they doubt the "lifetime" claims: they greet them skeptically. Their doubt is well founded, not unreasonable or hasty, and they aren't torn (ambivalent).

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: From fountains like Crown Fountain by Jaume Plensa, found at Millennium Park, to street art like Don’t Fret’s mural Gift To The Class of 2016 on South Wabash Avenue, Chicago offers an array of works to ______ the tastes of art lovers.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: A wide range of works is there to satisfy, or satiate, different tastes. Mitigate (lessen), venerate (revere) and supplant (replace) don't fit tastes.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Ethicist Ingrid Robeyns argues in her work that taxes on the very wealthy should be increased so that governments will be enabled to solve problems of collective action, such as mitigating climate change. Robeyns cites the work of economist Mariana Mazzucato, who shows that government subsidies are a more effective engine of innovation than private sector investments; in addition, government-funded innovations tend to lead to further developments in disparate fields (such as the United States mission to land a person on the moon, which accelerated developments in nutrition as well as communications).
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It summarizes the research of one scholar, then presents a study by another scholar that was inspired by the findings of that research.
It introduces a proposition by a scholar, then describes that scholar’s use of findings by another scholar to support that proposition.
It details the findings of a research project by one scholar, then puts forward the suggestions of another scholar for further investigation.
It offers a claim by a scholar, then uses the results of a project by another scholar to show why that claim should be rejected.

questions.explanation: Robeyns proposes higher taxes on the wealthy, then cites Mazzucato's findings to support it. Mazzucato's work isn't inspired by Robeyns's, and it supports the claim rather than rejecting it.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage:
Text 1

The novels of Henry James changed stylistically starting in 1902, becoming more demanding and featuring a much more measured pace than his earlier works. This places a burden on readers that they may not be prepared for: James’s late novels are some of the best he wrote, but they are not for everyone.

Text 2

The films of Martin Scorsese released starting in 2016 have the same place in his filmography that the late novels of Henry James have in his bibliography. Both are works by proven masters—James had published The American (1877); Scorsese had directed Mean Streets (1973)—who began to make demanding works, such as James’s The Wings of the Dove (1902) and Scorsese’s Silence (2016), that ask more of their audiences than their earlier works do but give more in return.
questions.prompt: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the underlined claim in Text 1?

choices.text: By arguing that James’s novels cannot be fully understood without also considering Scorsese’s films
By conceding that James’s The American is a superior novel to The Wings of the Dove
By asserting that both James and Scorsese ought to be considered masters of their chosen art forms
By agreeing that James’s late novels are excellent but can be challenging for their readers

questions.explanation: Text 2 says James's late works "ask more of their audiences" but "give more in return": demanding but rewarding, which agrees with Text 1's claim. C is true of Text 2 but isn't a response to the underlined claim, and nothing supports A or B.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage:
The following text is from Hilda Eunice Burgos’s 2018 novel Ana María Reyes Does Not Live in a Castle. The narrator is in sixth grade.

The next day I went to my piano lesson, as I did every Tuesday after school. My piano teacher, Doña Dulce Sánchez, lived two blocks from my school, in the opposite direction from my house.
questions.prompt: According to the text, where did the narrator’s piano teacher live?

choices.text: Two blocks from the narrator’s school
Across the street from the narrator’s home
One block from the narrator’s home

questions.explanation: The text says the teacher "lived two blocks from my school," in the opposite direction from the narrator's house.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Emulsification is a process that creates a uniform mixture that includes two ingredients that do not combine on their own, such as oil and water. For this process to happen, a third ingredient, an emulsifier, must be combined with the other two. Carrageenan, a substance extracted from red seaweed, is a common emulsifier: it helps to create a smooth texture in condensed milk that makes it more pleasant to drink.
questions.prompt: According to the text, what result is associated with carrageenan?

choices.text: It helps ensure that condensed milk has a smooth texture.
It prolongs the time it takes for ingredients to mix together during the making of condensed milk.
It decreases the amount of one ingredient in condensed milk while increasing the amount of another.
It assists in the evaporation of water during the making of condensed milk.

questions.explanation: The text says carrageenan "helps to create a smooth texture in condensed milk." Nothing is said about timing, amounts or evaporation.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Biologist Nathalie Stroeymeyt and her team found that black garden ants demonstrated a sophisticated form of “architectural immunity.” When confronted with fungal pathogens, these ants modified their excavation patterns in several strategic ways to speed up nest growth, increase spacing between entrances, and reduce the centrality of key chambers (containing the queen, food, or nursery). The team noted that these modifications weren’t random but specifically arranged to minimize fungal spread.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: A team of scientists noticed that fungal pathogen exposure causes black garden ants to abandon their existing nest structures.
According to a team of biologists, black garden ants build larger nests when exposed to a harmful fungus than they otherwise would build.
A study found that black garden ants deliberately modify their nest architecture to keep a harmful fungus from spreading.
A study noted that black garden ants exposed to a harmful fungus tend to dig longer tunnels in their nests instead of reducing the centrality of the nest’s chambers.

questions.explanation: The ants changed how they dig in deliberate ways "to minimize fungal spread." They don't abandon their nests, B covers only one detail, and D contradicts the text, which says they do reduce chambers' centrality.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Peter Pan is a 1911 novel by J.M. Barrie. In the fantasy novel, a young boy named Peter lives on a mythical island. The narrator indicates that Peter does not know that pretend things are not real: ______
questions.prompt: Which quotation about Peter from Peter Pan best supports the claim?

choices.text: “He boasted that he had gone walking for the good of his health.”
“He had fallen at once into a dreamless sleep.”
“In his absence things are usually quiet on the island.”
“To him make-believe and true were exactly the same thing.”

questions.explanation: D says outright that for Peter make-believe and real were the same, exactly the claim. The others say nothing about pretend things.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage:
A student is researching the Amstrad CPC and other important gaming systems that were part of the global rise of the home video game industry during the 1970s and 1980s. The student is surprised to find that the Amstrad CPC sold relatively few units worldwide, with only about ______

Home Video Game Systems of the 1970s and 1980s

\[table:[["System", "Manufacturer", "Approximate number of units sold worldwide"], ["Apple II", "Apple Inc.", "4,487,000"], ["Amstrad CPC", "Amstrad", "2,000,000"], ["Game & Watch", "Nintendo", "18,600,000"], ["Intellivision", "Mattel", "3,000,000"]]\]
questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?

choices.text: 2,000,000 units sold compared to the approximately 18,600,000 units sold of the Game & Watch.
3,000,000 units sold compared to the approximately 4,487,000 units sold of the Game & Watch.
2,000,000 units sold compared to the approximately 18,600,000 units sold of the Intellivision.
3,000,000 units sold compared to the approximately 4,487,000 units sold of the Apple II.

questions.explanation: The Amstrad CPC sold about 2,000,000 units and the Game & Watch about 18,600,000. B and D give the wrong figure for the Amstrad, and C pairs 18,600,000 with the wrong system.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Brittle stars are sea animals that move along the ocean floor using their five arms. Unlike most animals, brittle stars have 70%–80% of their weight in their arms. To better understand the benefits of this unusual trait, scientists built a soft robot inspired by the brittle star’s body structure. The robot has a middle disk and five arms whose weights can be changed. When the scientists made the arms heavier, the arms pressed down more firmly on the ground. This stronger grip kept the arms from slipping and allowed the robot to move more efficiently across the ocean floor. Based on these results, the scientists hypothesize that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: brittle stars have most of the weight in their arms because that is where they store nutrients.
brittle stars have most of their weight in their arms so they can scare off predators.
having most of their weight in their arms allows brittle stars to climb steep underwater cliffs.
having most of their weight in their arms helps brittle stars move across the ocean floor.

questions.explanation: Heavier arms gave the robot a better grip and more efficient movement across the ocean floor, so the scientists would hypothesize that the weight helps brittle stars move there. Nutrients, predators and cliffs aren't part of the experiment.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: The state of Maine has classified the smallmouth bass as an invasive species that could harm some of the state’s native species. But researchers Alejandro Camacho and Jason McLachlan have pointed out that Earth’s climate is changing in ways that challenge such classifications. Climate changes may force animals from their current ranges. Climate changes may also create good habitats in areas where a species couldn’t live previously. These observations suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Maine was previously home to some smallmouth bass but they were outcompeted by invading species.
it’s useful at present for Maine to distinguish between invasive and native species in some instances but not in the case of the smallmouth bass.
labels like the one that Maine has applied to the smallmouth bass reflect environmental conditions that may not persist.
even if Earth’s climate doesn’t change in the way scientists predict, the smallmouth bass will likely establish itself in Maine.

questions.explanation: If climate change shifts where species can live, an "invasive" label reflects today's conditions, which may change. The text gives no history of bass in Maine, doesn't single out the bass as an exception, and D ignores the climate point.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: A multifaceted constellation of environmental factors, including oceanic surface temperatures, tropospheric wind shear, and ambient atmospheric humidity, ______ the developmental trajectory and destructive potential of hurricanes before landfall.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular "constellation"; the list after "including" doesn't change that. A singular subject takes "dictates."

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: In the tapestries Blessing of Rain and Intended Vermillion, Diné textile artist D.Y. Begay uses ______ and yellows extracted from cochineal insects from Peru as well as local hollyhocks, coreopsis, and chamisa plants gathered from her Tsélání homeland in Arizona.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Reds, greens, and yellows" is a list of three, so each item before "and" is followed by a comma. A semicolon doesn't separate simple list items.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Although Spanish artist Pablo Picasso (1881–1973) is famous mainly for his paintings, he worked in other art forms as well. Picasso ______ experimenting with sculpture as a young man and eventually created hundreds of innovative pieces, many of which he kept in his home.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The sentence needs a main verb for "Picasso," parallel with "created": "began." The other choices aren't verbs that can stand alone.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Colonial American newspapers played an important role in protesting British taxes, such as those resulting from the Stamp Act in 1765. Publisher William Rind showed his opposition by printing skull and crossbones symbols ______ the front page of his newspaper, the Maryland Gazette, where tax stamps would normally go.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "On the front page" is one prepositional phrase, and nothing should separate a preposition from its object.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Rock carvings found on islands around the lower Susquehanna River in Maryland repeatedly feature the same stylized face. Experts are divided on whether the face represents the head of a ______ a human, or a mythical figure.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "A fish, a serpent, a human, or a mythical figure" is a list, so commas separate the items.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: In ancient China, the art of miniaturizing trees in containers was called “penjing.” This term, which means “potted scenery,” ______ in China.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject "This term" needs a main verb, and only "is still used" is one. "Still used" alone would read as a modifier, not a verb.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: A recent study ______ by biologists Brandi Pessman and Eileen Hebets at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln found that in noisy environments, some funnel-weaving spiders built webs that amplified the sound of incoming vibrations at a particular frequency, allowing the spiders “to better hear certain signals above the noise,” according to Pessman.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The sentence's main verb is "found," so the blank must describe the study: "a recent study conducted by…" Any full verb there would leave two main verbs.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Many cities invest in public art, displaying works in locations where they can be enjoyed by anyone. On display in Charlotte, North Carolina, ______ is a sculpture with rotating steel layers that align to form a human head.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The sculpture in Charlotte is an example of a city's public art, so "for instance" fits. There's no contrast or final step.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: In a 1993 study by Vales and Peek, the researchers used microhistological fecal analysis to determine the ratio of three plant subtypes (graminoids, forbs, and browse) within the diets of North American ungulates. The researchers did not perform this analysis on all such ungulates, ______ they focused exclusively on elk in Wyoming.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Focusing only on elk in Wyoming restates "did not perform this analysis on all such ungulates" in more specific terms, so "in other words" fits. Elk aren't one example among several studied, and there's no contrast.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Lalo Schifrin, an Argentine American composer and pianist who wrote and recorded a number of jazz albums with trumpeter Dizzy Gillespie in the 1960s, also composed music for many films and television shows. ______ Schifrin’s most iconic work, the theme for the 1966 TV show Mission: Impossible, uses a jazz-inspired 5/4 time signature.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: It's appropriate that a jazz musician's best-known TV theme uses a jazz-inspired time signature, so "Fittingly" fits. It isn't a contrast, a restatement or a correction.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: One might assume that the Netherlands’ Gemini offshore wind farm produces the same amount of energy as land-based wind farms of a similar size. ______ because wind speeds over open water are generally higher than those over land, Gemini’s turbines turn faster and produce more energy than do most land farms’ turbines.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The second sentence corrects the assumption in the first: Gemini produces more energy, not the same. "Actually" signals that correction.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage:
• The Highpointers Club is a hiking club.
• One of the main goals among club members is to reach the highest points in all fifty US states.
• Those who achieve this are called 50 Completers.
• In Suk Han became a 50 Completer on November 15, 2013.
• The highest point in Wisconsin is Timms Hill, at 1,951 ft.
• The highest point in Wyoming is Gannett Peak, at 13,809 ft.
questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to explain the 50 Completers hiking challenge to a new audience?

choices.text: If you are looking for a new hiking challenge, consider joining the Highpointers Club, as did In Suk Han, a hiker who successfully reached the highest point in every US state.

Not until after you have reached the highest points in all fifty US states—including Timms Hill in Wisconsin and Gannett Peak in Wyoming—can you include yourself among the 50 Completers of the Highpointers Club.
On November 15, 2013, In Suk Han finally completed the feat of reaching the highest point in all fifty US states, including Timms Hill in Wisconsin and Gannett Peak in Wyoming.
Hikers aiming to count themselves among the 50 Completers must reach not only Wisconsin’s Timms Hill but also the even higher peak of Gannett Peak in Wyoming.

questions.explanation: B names the challenge, says what it takes (the highest points in all fifty states) and gives examples. A and C describe one hiker without naming the 50 Completers challenge, and D makes it sound like only two peaks are needed.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage:
While researching asteroid 16 Psyche, a student gathered the following notes:
• Asteroid 16 Psyche orbits the Sun within the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
• The majority of known asteroids are composed primarily of rocky silicate minerals, ice, or carbonaceous matter.
• Psyche is exceptionally dense and consists almost entirely of metallic iron and nickel.
• Scientists hypothesize that Psyche may be the exposed metallic core of an early protoplanet.
questions.prompt: The student wants to emphasize the unique composition of asteroid 16 Psyche compared to other asteroids. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: Orbiting between Mars and Jupiter, asteroid 16 Psyche was the target of an exploratory mission launched by NASA.
Unlike typical asteroids composed mainly of silicates, ice, or carbon, 16 Psyche consists almost entirely of metallic iron and nickel.
Most asteroids in the main belt contain rocky silicates, though scientists study multiple compositions to investigate planetary formation.
Scientists hypothesize that Psyche may represent the exposed core of an early protoplanet due to its high density.

questions.explanation: B contrasts what Psyche is made of with what most asteroids are made of. A is about its orbit, C doesn't mention Psyche's makeup, and D is about a hypothesis rather than a comparison.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Waiting is a 1987 black-and-white linocut print by Kuwaiti artist Thuraya Al-Baqsami.
• It depicts a tranquil, everyday scene (a woman in a headscarf looking out a window).
• ¡Sera toda nuestra! (“It will all be ours!”) is a 1977 color linocut print by Mexican American artist Carlos Cortéz.
• It features a scene with an explicitly political point of view (a group of laborers preparing to go on strike).
• Relief printing is a technique in which an image is carved onto a printing block, covered in ink or paint, and stamped onto paper.
• Linocut is a type of relief printing that uses linoleum tile as the printing block.
questions.prompt: The student wants to contrast the subject matter of the two prints. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: Cortéz made ¡Sera toda nuestra! (“It will all be ours!”) in 1977, while Al-Baqsami made Waiting later, in 1987.
The scenes depicted in both works were first carved onto a printing block, then stamped onto paper; however, one work is a linocut, while the other is a relief print.
Cortéz’s print expresses an explicitly political point of view, while Al-Baqsami’s depicts a tranquil, everyday scene.
The print by Cortéz is a color linocut; by contrast, Al-Baqsami’s is a relief print.

questions.explanation: Subject matter is what the prints show: C contrasts a political scene with a tranquil, everyday one. A contrasts dates, and B and D contrast technique, inaccurately, since both are linocuts and so both are relief prints.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Weather patterns, market trends, input costs, labor availability, equipment maintenance, and biological cycles are all variables that farmers must consider separately and in terms of how they may affect each other, and it is this ______ of factors in particular that makes successful farm management so challenging.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Factors that "affect each other" are in interplay, and "in particular" points back to that interaction as the challenge. Neglect, misinterpretation and resolution aren't described.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: To maximize ______, package distribution centers employ advanced scheduling systems and strategic staging areas that allow for goods received from warehouses to be immediately transferred to trucks for delivery to their final destinations. Some centers are so efficient that even the largest delivery trucks can be filled in a matter of minutes.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Moving goods straight from arrival onto trucks, and filling trucks in minutes, maximizes throughput: how much passes through. Centers wouldn't aim to maximize overhead or liability, and staffing isn't discussed.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Researchers have developed algorithms that take into account how various ______ influence production schedules, allowing rapid solution generation for manufacturing planning problems. The algorithms help identify efficient production schedules by processing those quantifiable inputs (e.g., demand patterns and capacity constraints) without exhaustively testing all possible scenarios.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: "Those quantifiable inputs" refers back to the blank, and inputs such as demand patterns and capacity constraints are parameters.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Marvel Girl’s ability to lift modest loads with her mind is illustrative of the lamentably lackluster powers bestowed on many female superheroes, but even those with more formidable powers have been subject to unflattering portrayals that often serve as ______: as the Phoenix, Jean Grey loses control of a cosmic force and destroys an entire planet, showing the corrupting influence of power.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: A story showing "the corrupting influence of power" is a warning, an admonition. The portrayal is unflattering, so it isn't a veneration or an exoneration, and it clarifies rather than obscures.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Research on minor solar eruptions in magnetically quiet regions revealed an interesting pattern. Material expelled during these events follows a narrow arc trajectory back to the Sun’s surface. High-resolution images show these eruptions produce thin streams of hot gas moving at speeds between 55 and 200 kilometers per second. Although these are impressive speeds, they are not sufficient to overcome the confining forces of the Sun’s gravity and magnetic field, so the material is pulled back down.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.text: It describes a natural phenomenon that is explained later in the text.
It presents a research finding that challenges the view mentioned in the first sentence of the text.
It acknowledges an exception to the pattern described in the first sentence of the text.
It discusses a natural occurrence that leads to the consequences explained later in the text.

questions.explanation: The underlined sentence describes the pattern (material arcing back to the Sun), and the last sentence explains why: the gas isn't fast enough to escape gravity and the magnetic field. It is the pattern, not an exception or a challenge to it, and what follows explains its cause rather than its consequences.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: With examples ranging from Dean’s Blue Hole in the Bahamas to Watling’s Blue Hole near San Salvador Island, blue holes are large underwater sinkholes: pits filled with dark blue water that contrasts with lighter blue shallower waters surrounding them. The formation of blue holes typically involves several natural processes, including the dissolution of limestone or other soluble rocks. Currently, the deepest blue hole on record is the Taam Ja’ Blue Hole in Chetumal Bay, Mexico, which is reported by Laura Carrillo and colleagues as extending at least 420 meters below sea level.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes the appearance of a particular type of sinkhole, compares the formations of two sinkholes of that type, and then names the researchers who discovered the deepest known sinkhole of that type.
It compares a deep sinkhole to a shallower one, details the processes by which both sinkholes formed, and emphasizes the remarkable depth of the deeper sinkhole.
It explains how a particular sinkhole formed, evaluates that sinkhole’s unusual appearance, and names a research team that is studying the sinkhole.
It defines a kind of sinkhole, describes its typical appearance and formation, and provides information about the deepest known sinkhole.

questions.explanation: The text defines blue holes and their look, explains how they typically form, then gives the deepest one on record. It never compares the formation of two particular holes, and Carrillo's team reported the depth rather than discovering the hole.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage:
Text 1 is from George Eliot’s 1860 novel The Mill on the Floss. Text 2 is from Rabindranath Tagore’s 1921 nonfiction book Glimpses of Bengal.

Text 1

The wood I walk in on this mild May day, with the young yellow-brown foliage of the oaks between me and the blue sky, the white star-flowers and the blue-eyed speedwell and the ground ivy at my feet, what grove of tropic palms, what strange ferns or splendid broad-petalled blossoms, could ever thrill such deep and delicate fibres within me as this home scene?

Text 2

My feelings seem to be those of our ancient earth in the daily ecstasy of its sun-kissed life; my own consciousness seems to stream through each blade of grass, each sucking root, to rise with the sap through the trees, to break out with joyous thrills in the waving fields of corn, in the rustling palm leaves.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes a notable difference in how the references to palm trees function in Text 1 and Text 2?

choices.text: While the narrator of Text 1 and the author of Text 2 both refer to metaphorical palm trees, only the narrator of Text 1 suggests that the palm trees are representative of home.

While palm trees form part of a series conveying the variety of the natural world in both texts, only the author of Text 2 recognizes how closely interconnected palm trees are with other plants in their environment.

While the narrator of Text 1 and the author of Text 2 both discuss palm trees to suggest the value of experiencing the natural world, only the narrator of Text 1 alludes to the labor that goes into cultivating real palm trees.
While palm trees serve to evoke natural beauty in both texts, only the author of Text 2 expresses a close sense of identification with palm trees.

questions.explanation: In both texts palms call up natural beauty, but Tagore feels his own consciousness streaming into the palm leaves, a close identification, while Eliot's narrator says tropic palms can't move him like his home scene. The palms in Text 1 are the opposite of home, and neither text mentions cultivating them.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Primarily encountered by modern readers as inert written texts, the vernacular riddles of early medieval England contain “implicit vestiges” of an interactive performance context, scholar Jill Frederick argues. Locative phrases (e.g., “here” and “now”) scattered throughout the riddles indicate the space shared by their speakers and audiences; the common refrain “say what I am called” invites a verbalized response; and the conflation of many of the riddles’ speakers with their solutions (typically animals, objects, or natural phenomena) suggests a form of dramatic impersonation perhaps meant to entertain during public gatherings.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: It is reasonable to conclude based on textual evidence from the vernacular riddles of early medieval England that they were mainly performed at large public gatherings, though documentation of the locations in which they were performed is unlikely to exist.

Linguistic evidence found within the vernacular riddles of early medieval England suggests that they may have been intended to be performed in communal settings, though this isn’t how they are generally experienced by readers today.

People of early medieval England likely found that era’s vernacular riddles to be more amusing than modern readers do, given that there is substantial evidence to indicate that they are best experienced in the context of an interactive performance rather than exclusively as written texts.

Scholars once assumed that the vernacular riddles of early medieval England were originally intended to be read silently, but newly uncovered historical documents corroborate Jill Frederick’s assertion that they may in fact have been intended primarily for oral performance.

questions.explanation: Frederick points to wording in the riddles ("here," "say what I am called," speakers as their solutions) as signs they were performed for audiences, while today they're read as written texts. A overstates ("mainly … large public gatherings"), C compares amusement, which the text doesn't, and D invents new documents.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: In the Mexican dialect of Spanish, the consonant s is pronounced with greater tension in the tongue than it is in Castilian, the dominant dialect in Spain, resulting in a sharper sound. Margarita Hidalgo, a linguist at San Diego State University, argues that Mexican Spanish acquired this pronunciation from Nahuatl, the language of the Nahua people in central Mexico: as the Spanish colonizers of Mexico incorporated Nahuatl words into their speech, and as more and more Nahuas spoke Spanish as a second language, the Nahuatl pronunciation of the s consonant replaced the Castilian pronunciation.
questions.prompt: Information in the text best supports which statement about the consonant s?

choices.text: The pronunciation of this consonant is the principal difference between the Mexican and Castilian dialects of Spanish.
This consonant appears in a higher percentage of Nahuatl vocabulary than of Castilian vocabulary.
The pronunciation of this consonant in Nahuatl may have been affected by its pronunciation in Mexican Spanish.
The pronunciation of this consonant requires greater tension in the tongue in Nahuatl than in Castilian.

questions.explanation: Mexican Spanish's s has more tongue tension than Castilian's, and it came from Nahuatl, so Nahuatl's s must also have more tension than Castilian's. The text doesn't call it the principal difference or compare frequencies, and C reverses the direction of influence.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Cover crops, such as teff, are planted by many farmers between main growing seasons. While these crops are known for increasing biodiversity, Axel Don and his coauthor argued in a 2015 study that cover crops’ role in supporting soil carbon sequestration deserves more attention. Cover crops remove carbon dioxide (CO₂) from the air and convert it to organic compounds; some of these compounds are stored in the soil as soil organic carbon (SOC), which contributes to the buildup of SOC stocks over time. Based on data from numerous farm fields, Don and his coauthor concluded that cover crops contribute meaningfully to soil carbon sequestration and, if widely adopted, could help offset agricultural emissions of atmospheric CO₂ and other greenhouse gases.
questions.prompt: Which finding, if true, would be most consistent with Don and his coauthor’s conclusion?

choices.text: Teff captures considerably more CO₂ in fields where it is the sole cover crop compared with fields where it is grown alongside other species of cover crops.
Cover crops generally exhibit reduced carbon sequestration rates in fields exposed to high levels of greenhouse gas emissions compared with fields exposed to low levels of those emissions.
SOC stocks vary more in fields where cover crops have been grown for decades compared with fields where cover crops have only recently been introduced.
SOC stocks tend to be significantly lower in fields without cover crops compared with fields where cover crops have been grown for several years.

questions.explanation: If cover crops add meaningfully to soil carbon, fields with them for years should hold more SOC than fields without them, which is D. A compares growing teff alone or mixed, B suggests they work worse where emissions are high, and C is about variability, not amount.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: While the brain regions most strongly associated with language tasks have some modularity in that different language tasks activate these areas to varying degrees, comprehension also invokes other areas of the brain more strongly associated with nonlinguistic functions. For example, understanding a description of a person performing physical actions might call on parts of the listener’s brain associated with sensory-motor functions, whereas a highly emotive account will likely activate areas associated with affective processing. Thus, beyond the areas most strongly associated with linguistic functions, ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: the specific combination of brain regions involved in comprehending speech is likely contingent on the total context in which the speech is embedded.
the brain regions associated with sensory-motor functions are often involved in general comprehension, even in contexts that don’t involve descriptions of physical movement.

the brain regions most strongly associated with affective processing activate whenever a listener believes an utterance has emotional connotations, even if the speaker did not intend those connotations.

the areas of the brain that activate when processing speech will typically include areas primarily responsible for nonlinguistic functions, although the exact combination of areas may be impossible to determine.

questions.explanation: The examples show different content calling on different brain areas (physical actions, sensory-motor; emotion, affective), so which areas are involved depends on the context. B and C go beyond the examples, and nothing suggests the combination can't be determined.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: The Clarion-Clipperton Zone (CCZ) is an expanse of abyssal plain and seamounts (underwater mountains) between Hawai‘i and Mexico in which mining is permitted, but the area’s biodiversity is poorly understood. The vast majority of invertebrate species found in a recent survey of the CCZ were hitherto unknown to scientists, and sampling for animal life has been highly concentrated in the eastern part of the zone. Some species like Psychropotes dyscrita were identified both morphologically and molecularly (using DNA analysis), whereas Discantenna metallica and other species for which molecular sampling was impracticable were identified solely based on physical morphology. Since molecular analysis does not require distinguishing subtle physiological differences, it is ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: more frequently used for identifying species with physiological characteristics like those of Psychropotes dyscrita than morphological analysis is.
capable of providing greater physiological detail about a species than is the method used for Discantenna metallica.
better suited to distinguishing Discantenna metallica from morphologically similar species than to distinguishing Psychropotes dyscrita from morphologically similar species.
more likely to properly distinguish between morphologically similar but distinct invertebrate species than is the method used to identify Discantenna metallica.

questions.explanation: Morphological identification depends on spotting subtle physical differences; DNA analysis doesn't, so it's better at telling apart species that look alike, better than the morphology-only method used for Discantenna metallica. B gets it backwards (DNA analysis isn't about physiological detail), and nothing supports A or C.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage:
Text 1

Paleontologists historically hypothesized that sauropod dinosaurs held their long necks vertically aloft like modern giraffes, allowing them to browse undisturbed foliage at the tops of towering forest canopies.

Text 2

Biomechanical simulations conducted by Dr. Raymond Kent suggest that sauropod cervical vertebrae lacked the dorsal articulation required for sustained vertical posture. Kent asserts that sauropods instead swept their necks horizontally to forage broad swaths of low vegetation with minimal locomotion.
questions.prompt: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the hypothesis discussed in Text 1?

choices.text: By arguing that giraffes and sauropods share identical vertebral morphology.
By disputing the claim that sauropods sustained a predominantly vertical neck orientation.
By demonstrating that sauropods relied entirely on high-canopy gymnosperms for nutrition.
By showing that sauropod neck fossils are too degraded for accurate biomechanical modeling.

questions.explanation: Kent's simulations show the vertebrae couldn't hold a vertical posture for long, and that sauropods swept their necks horizontally, which disputes Text 1's vertical-neck hypothesis.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Rare species advantage (RSA) describes the situation in which there are few conspecifics (other members of the same species) in an organism’s immediate surroundings, enabling the organism to avoid competition with conspecifics for the same resources; RSA is widely believed to play a crucial role in maintaining ecological stability. Among tree species in the Barro Colorado Island plot (latitude 9.15° N) and other tropical forest sites, there is little correlation between conspecific aggregation and the abundance of a given species in the wider local area, so RSA is expected, but in the Fenglin Nature Reserve (latitude 48.08° N) and other temperate forest sites, the aggregation-abundance correlation for tree species is strongly negative. Mathematical modeling suggests, however, that ecological niche distinction may mitigate the apparent risk to temperate ecological stability engendered by this pattern: ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: as a tree species in temperate forests becomes more abundant, individuals of that species are more likely to be found near conspecifics, enabling abundant species to exploit localized resources to a greater extent than rare species can.

even though rare tree species in temperate forests tend to cluster with conspecifics more than rare tree species in tropical forests do, they are sufficiently rare locally that they benefit from RSA more than rare tropical species do.
although rare tree species in temperate forests encounter relatively high local competition from conspecifics, they can thrive by exploiting resources that are underexploited by other local species.

while an increase in abundance in one tree species often leads to a reduction in abundance of nearby species, temperate tree species tend to play different roles in the same ecosystem, reducing the expected effect of abundance on aggregation.

questions.explanation: A strongly negative correlation means rare temperate species cluster with their own kind, so they lose RSA and face competition from conspecifics. Niche distinction would help by letting them use resources other species leave alone, which is C. A contradicts the negative correlation, B contradicts the loss of RSA, and D doesn't address the risk to rare species.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: A premortem is an exercise in which teams imagine their project has already failed, then brainstorm possible reasons for that failure. Despite its apparent pessimism, ______ prompting teams to proactively develop mitigation strategies during the planning stage. As a result, the project is more likely to succeed.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.text: effective uncovering of potential problems by the team in this activity is done early,
this activity effectively uncovers potential problems early,
potential problems are effectively uncovered by this activity early,
teams effectively uncover potential problems early with this activity,

questions.explanation: "Despite its apparent pessimism" describes the premortem, so the subject right after the comma must be the activity itself: "this activity." The other choices make the uncovering, the problems or the teams the thing with pessimism.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: The trailblazing achievements of Roger Bannister, the English track star famous for breaking the four-minute-mile barrier at Oxford’s Iffley Road Track in 1954, ______ confined to the realm of athletics: Bannister also became a pioneering neurologist in the field of autonomic disorders—conditions affecting involuntary nervous system responses—and established the field’s first specialized scientific journal.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject is the plural "achievements," so it needs the plural "weren't." The other choices are singular.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: As one of aviation’s earliest female stunt performers, Gladys Ingle developed a versatile repertoire of acrobatic feats. Her specialized skills included standing on the wing of a flying aircraft and shooting a bow and arrow at a ______ perfect balance during aerial maneuvers, such as vertical loops; and even walking across the wing as an aircraft flew at full speed beneath a bridge.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The list items contain commas ("maneuvers, such as"), so the items are separated with semicolons, matching the semicolon already before "and even walking."

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: During a recent investigation, archaeologists ______ an explanation for the consistent and seemingly deliberate placement of petroglyphs (rock carvings) near water analyzed several sites on Caribbean islands. They discovered that many of the pools near petroglyphs had consistent water levels year-round, creating perfect reflecting surfaces for the carved symbols on the rocks.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The main verb is "analyzed," so the blank must describe the archaeologists: "archaeologists seeking an explanation … analyzed." A finite verb in the blank would leave two main verbs.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: For his mash-up “Smells Like Rockin’ Robin,” DJ Mark Vidler layered Kurt Cobain’s minor-key vocals from “Smells Like Teen Spirit” over the Jackson 5’s major-key blues progression from “Rockin’ ______ by inserting the grunge singer’s vocal melody as pitch-shifted “blue notes” within the pop-soul group’s harmonic framework, creates an intensified “bluesy” sound and subverts the expectations of listeners familiar with either musical source.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "A technique that … creates" is a long appositive with its own interrupting phrase ("by inserting … framework"), which needs a comma after "that" to match the one after "framework." A dash sets the appositive off from the main clause; B and C would leave it a fragment.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Named for the year in which it was detected by English astronomers, SN 2016aps was a supernova (the explosion of a massive ______ in the constellation Draco, 3.6 billion light-years from Earth, the transient yet powerful blast propelled particles and debris into space at extremely high speeds.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The first sentence is complete once the parenthesis closes. "Occurring in the constellation Draco … the blast propelled…" is a new sentence, so a period goes after the parenthesis. Joining them makes a run-on.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Originating during the Cretaceous period, ______
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.text: entomologists have extensively examined fossilized resin deposits excavated in northern Myanmar.
the fossilized amber specimens excavated in northern Myanmar preserve unprecedented anatomical details of early arthropods.
paleontological excavation in northern Myanmar has uncovered numerous ancient arthropods.
arthropods were trapped and entombed within sticky conifer secretions.

questions.explanation: Whatever comes right after the comma is what originated in the Cretaceous. That's the amber specimens, not entomologists or an excavation. D is grammatical but doesn't fit as well: the modifier describes the preserved specimens, which B names.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: The Hornbostel-Sachs system classifies musical instruments by how they produce sound. For example, an instrument that is popular in India called the saraswati veena produces sound primarily through the vibration of its strings. ______ under the Hornbostel-Sachs system, the saraswati veena is a chordophone.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Because the veena makes sound with vibrating strings, it follows that it is classed as a chordophone. "Thus" marks that conclusion.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: India’s prominence as a supplier of information technology services to companies in North America and Europe is a result of several factors, including the country’s investments in technical education, but the most serendipitous is India’s large number of English speakers. English is spoken by more people in India—129 million—than in any nation except the US. ______ only about 10% of Indians speak English.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.text: However, English is not the first language for most English speakers in India:
Granted, this numerical advantage is due more to population size than to language penetration:
As a result, careers in information technology services are not available to all people in India:
Accordingly, 90% of people in India—over one billion people—do not speak the language:

questions.explanation: "Only about 10% of Indians speak English" explains that the large number comes from India's huge population, not from widespread English. B concedes exactly that, and the colon leads into the figure. The others don't connect to the 10% statistic.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: On June 13, 1927, aviator Charles Lindbergh received a ticker-tape parade in New York City in recognition of his transatlantic flight. Of the 206 ticker-tape parades held between 1886 and 2022, a notable number were for achievements in aviation. ______ Lindbergh’s parade was just one of 16 honoring pilots.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The last sentence backs up "a notable number" with a figure (16), confirming and strengthening the point, so "Indeed" fits.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage: Between February 1876 and September 1876, George Eliot’s novel Daniel Deronda was serialized in eight parts in Blackwood’s Magazine. Scholars typically regard the serial version of Eliot’s novel as less authoritative than the version later published in book form. ______ as scholar Philip Allingham notes, serialized texts were the versions in which the nineteenth-century readership first “saw itself and its world reflected, and to which it responded, often with great emotion.”
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.text: Accordingly, they emphasize the appeal of the serial version for Victorian audiences;
Still, the serial version is important to an understanding of the novel’s historical context;
Consequently, the book version of the novel is often favored over the serial version;
However, others regard the serial version as a more faithful representation of Eliot’s intentions;

questions.explanation: Allingham's point is that readers of the time first met and responded to the novel in its serial form, which makes the serial version important historically despite being less authoritative. B introduces exactly that. Allingham's quote is about readers, not Eliot's intentions.

questions.subject: reading-writing
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Enhanced rock weathering (ERW) is a method of spreading crushed basalt on farmland to capture carbon dioxide (CO₂) and improve soil health.
• ERW increases crop yields and removes harmful CO₂ from the air.
• ERW offers a low-cost, low-tech alternative to expensive, energy-intensive carbon capture methods.
• The CO₂ captured by ERW becomes stable bicarbonate in soil water, which eventually streams into the ocean to remain safely stored for hundreds of years.
• ERW can improve rural economies by reducing farmers’ need for fertilizers and increasing their earnings from carbon credits.
questions.prompt: The student wants to explain why ERW is a superior method for capturing CO₂. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: ERW improves soil health and helps farmers increase their income from selling carbon credits.
ERW removes CO₂ from the air in a way that is both low-cost and low-tech.
The CO₂ captured by ERW becomes stable bicarbonate, which improves soil health by remaining in the ocean for hundreds of years.
ERW is a method of spreading crushed basalt on farmland to capture CO₂, improving rural economies.

questions.explanation: Calling ERW superior for capturing CO₂ means comparing it with other capture methods: it's cheap and low-tech where they're expensive and energy-intensive. A and D are about farming benefits, and C muddles the facts.
